move to the end of file (like other file/dissector)

Hi. Thanks for your feedback. However, I prefer to keep this table before the functions for a better readability, because it is used both to build the hf table (see proto_register_FiveCoRAP) and directly by the dissector. Indeed, unlike most dissectors, this one can potentially be extended by adding rows to this table and without changing the code.

it is not possible to use tvb_get_ipv4 ? (and tvb_get_ether ?)

Maybe yes but with type casting since tvb_get_ipv4 returns a guint32 and not a byte array. I would like to keep the current the text displayed in the tree. Is there a function to transform guint32 ip address to string (same question for MAC address)?
yes, there is tvb_ip_to_str
Ok thanks. I will try to change that.

I prefer to keep this information (Interface number, timeout and frame size) on a single line in the tree to keep it compact. With an hf entry, this data would be on several lines.

Is dissect_frame guaranteed to advance tcp_data_offset?
Really good point. Sorry for this big mistake. Latest commit corrects this.
If this is recursive, you might want to add a p_set_proto_depth/p_get_proto_depth check or something similar.

As far that I understand those functions, they can be used only for single instance recursive protocol. In this one, there can be up to 8 subdevices which all can also have 8 subdevices and so on. This dissector can dissect up to MAX_SUB_DEVICES regardless of the depth.

Please move to the end to follow the structure of other dissectors.

Unlike other dissectors, this one is based on an evolving table (registers_def). The list of header fields is therefore stored in two arrays of constants loaded in the hf structure per code rather than statically as in other dissectors. This allows to access the array data (especially their size) in the dissector code without defining twice the same information, which would be a source of bug in case of modification.
I can indeed move the definition of the arrays before the proto_register_FiveCoRAP function if that is what you suggest, but not integrate them as a static load in this function. Would this be the desired solution?
